label: Nonparametric Bayes on Manifolds
notes: This long chapter spans printed pages 156 to 181 and builds a Bayesian density estimator for data living on a curved manifold. We replace a single parametric model with a flexible mixture of kernels and place a Dirichlet process prior over the mixing distribution, then certify that the posterior concentrates at the true density.

label: Why Density Estimation on a Manifold
notes: Shape coordinates and directional data live on spheres or quotient manifolds, not Euclidean space, so ordinary kernel density estimation distorts distances and mass. We want a fully Bayesian density that respects the metric, supports multiple modes, and quantifies uncertainty about the whole density, not just a single Frechet mean.

label: Location-Concentration Kernels
notes: The building block is a parametric kernel indexed by a location on the manifold and a concentration controlling spread. On the sphere the complex Watson and Bingham kernels play this role, peaking at their location parameter and tightening as concentration grows, giving a smooth probability bump anchored to a manifold point.

label: The Mixture Density
notes: A flexible density is an integral of the kernel against a mixing measure over location and concentration. With a discrete mixing measure this becomes a weighted sum of kernels, so countably many bumps at different manifold locations build an arbitrarily rich multimodal density that still integrates to one against the manifold volume measure.

label: Dirichlet Process Prior
notes: We place a Dirichlet process prior on the mixing distribution, parameterized by a precision and a base measure on the parameter space. The Dirichlet process is the canonical nonparametric prior over distributions: it is conjugate under sampling, almost surely discrete, and gives full support over candidate mixing measures.

label: Stick-Breaking Weights
notes: Sethuraman's stick-breaking construction makes the prior explicit. We break a unit stick by independent Beta fractions, producing a decreasing sequence of weights that sum to one, each attached to an atom drawn from the base measure. This shows concretely why Dirichlet process draws are discrete with countably many atoms.

label: Polya Urn and Clustering
notes: Marginalizing the mixing measure yields the Polya urn, or Chinese restaurant, prediction rule. A new observation joins an existing cluster with probability proportional to its current size or starts a fresh cluster with probability proportional to the precision, inducing an automatic, data-driven number of mixture components.

label: Posterior Computation
notes: Posterior sampling uses Gibbs and blocked samplers. The Polya urn gives a collapsed Gibbs scheme that cycles cluster labels, while truncated stick-breaking enables blocked samplers updating weights and atoms jointly. Each sweep yields one posterior draw of the density, and averaging draws estimates the predictive density on the manifold.

label: Kullback-Leibler Support
notes: Consistency rests on a support condition: the true density must lie in the Kullback-Leibler support of the prior, meaning the prior places positive mass on every neighborhood where the average log-ratio to the truth is small. Continuous, fully supported densities are reached by mixtures, so this condition holds broadly.

label: Weak Posterior Consistency
notes: Schwartz's theorem delivers weak consistency: if the truth is in the prior's Kullback-Leibler support, the posterior mass of every weak neighborhood of the true density tends to one almost surely as the sample size grows. The kernel mixture prior on the manifold satisfies the hypotheses, so weak consistency holds.

label: Strong Posterior Consistency
notes: Strengthening to the total variation, or strong, topology needs entropy control. Combining the Kullback-Leibler support condition with sieves of bounded metric entropy and exponentially small prior tails, the posterior concentrates in strong neighborhoods of the true density, so the estimated density converges in total variation distance.

label: Estimating Means and Modes
notes: Consistency of the density transfers to functionals. The Frechet mean and the modes computed from the estimated density converge to those of the truth, and antimodes separate clusters. This certifies that Bayesian density estimation also yields consistent location summaries and a principled clustering of the manifold data.

label: Recap and Workflow
notes: The workflow is one arc: pick manifold kernels, place a Dirichlet process prior on the mixing measure, sample the posterior by Gibbs or blocked methods, and read off a consistent density, Frechet mean, modes, and clusters. The support and entropy conditions are what guarantee the posterior finds the truth.
